notes.meaning: John points back to Jesus, the Word of life, who existed before time began. The apostles were eyewitnesses who heard His voice, watched Him with their own eyes, and touched Him with their hands. This shows that the eternal Son of God became a real human being and was not just a spirit or ghost.

Jesus, who is life itself, was with the Father from eternity and stepped into human history. The apostles saw Him during His earthly life and proclaimed what they witnessed. He makes God's own eternal life available to everyone who believes in Him.

The apostles shared what they saw and heard so that others could enter into spiritual fellowship with them. Fellowship means sharing a common life together as a family of faith. This bond unites believers with one another because they are united with God the Father and His Son, Jesus Christ.

John wrote these truths so that the joy of believers would be complete. Real joy is not based on earthly circumstances, but on having a close relationship with God. When Christians share this life together, their joy overflows.

The main message the apostles heard from Jesus is that God is light. Light represents God's absolute holiness, truth, and purity, with no evil or falsehood mixed in. Because God is completely pure, darkness and sin have no place in Him at all.

Anyone who claims to share life with God while choosing a lifestyle of sin is not telling the truth. Since God is pure light, people cannot walk in moral darkness and still enjoy close communion with Him. Our everyday choices reveal whether our faith is real.

differ.view: Walking in darkness describes a true Christian who is temporarily living in disobedience and has broken daily fellowship with God, without losing salvation.
A lifestyle of walking in darkness shows that a person has never been truly born again, because God's grace always changes how someone lives.

notes.meaning: Walking in the light means living openly before God in honesty and obedience, guided by His Word. When Christians live in this light, they experience true unity with one another. Even though believers still make mistakes, the blood of Jesus constantly cleanses them from every sin.

Anyone who claims to be free from an inner sinful nature is merely fooling themselves. Even after coming to faith, Christians still struggle with remaining sin in this earthly life. Pretending to be sinless keeps God's truth from doing its work in our hearts.

differ.view: This warning applies before being cleansed by Christ, because His blood and Spirit can fully remove sin from the believer's heart in this life.
Every believer continues to carry an inner sinful nature throughout this life, so claiming to be entirely sinless is always self-deception.

notes.meaning: Confessing our sins means honestly agreeing with God about our wrongdoing and asking for His mercy. God is faithful to His promises and completely just, because Jesus paid our penalty on the cross. On that basis, He pardons our guilt and purifies our hearts from all wrongdoing.

Claiming that we have never committed acts of sin is an insult to God that treats Him like a liar. The Scriptures clearly state that every human being has sinned and fallen short of His holy standards. Anyone who refuses to admit their personal guilt shows that God's Word has no place in their life.
